# Types of Potentially Mitigatable Activity

The NHS is always seeking to reduce the volume of care needed in hospitals.
Forecasts of future activity demand would not be credible if they were unable
to take into account the predicted effects of interventions Trusts plan to 
implement.

In order to incorporate the predicted effects of such plans, the OpenPlan demand
model uses the concept of Types of Potentially Mitigatable Activity (TPMAs) to 
help define these predictions in a transparent and logical way.

The user is asked to identify the most appropriate TPMA that describes the activity
a chosen intervention should affect, and to describe their assumptions about how
much less activity they expect to be delivering in their horizon year, should their
plans be successful.

They do this by providing a range that represents the proportion of the activity
in the baseline year that would be plausible - an 80% prediction interval.
For example, if the estimated activity mitigation for 'Admission Avoidance: Cancelled Operations' is given as a prediction interval of 50%-70%, this means that users are 80% sure that that the number of cancelled operations will be reduced by between 30-50% in the horizon year, as compared with the baseline.

A value of 100% means no change, whilst one of 0% means that all activity is mitigated.

Each TPMA is defined based on clinical and operational evidence and/or expert
knowledge, and the full set are reviewed on a rolling basis.
All TPMAs are age-sex standardised to maximise their comparability across settings.
You can read about [how we standardise the data](../technical/modelling_methodology/activity_mitigators/direct_standardisation_of_tpmas.qmd) in the methodology section.

:::{.callout-important}
TPMA assumptions are specific to a particular set of baseline and horizon years.
Should you wish to use a different baseline or horizon year, you should always
carefully consider whether your TPMA assumptions are still valid.
:::


## Mechanisms of mitigation

Each TPMA is assigned to one of four mitigation mechanisms:

1. **Prevention** and public health initiatives. 

This includes hospital activity related to smoking, alcohol consumption, obesity or falls which may be deemed to be avoidable via prevention and public health interventions.

2. **Redirection/Substitution**.

Redirection of activity to out-of-hospital settings or the substitution of hospital activity for some alternative out-of-hospital intervention. 
This includes ambulatory care sensitive admissions, mental health admissions that may be avoided with psychiatric liaison, admissions of frail older people and low acuity admissions.

3. **De-adoption** 

De-adoption of low value activities, such as tonsillectomies, grommets, and unnecessary follow-up outpatient attendances.

4. **Efficiency**

Efficiency TPMAs describe types of activity that are not expected to reduce the 
number of admissions, but may reduce length of stay.


The full list of current TPMAs can be found in the relevant section:

- [Inpatient-related](/overview/inpatient_tpmas.qmd)
- [Outpatient-related](/overview/outpatient_tpmas.qmd)
- [A&E related](/overview/ae_tpmas.qmd)

A [lookup table](/overview/tpmas_lookup.qmd) is also available that contains an interactive table with a sortable and searchable lookup of OpenPlan types of potentially mitigatable activity (OpenPlan TPMAs).
